metadata.rules_text:
- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to under-forecast sharp upward moves; adjust forecast upward by 2–5% for the next 3–5 days.
- After a spike in price (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often over-estimates continuation; reduce forecast by 3–8% for next 5–10 days to allow for mean reversion.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive mid-period, model often fails to catch the momentum; increase forecast by 1–3% for next 3–7 days.
- Model under-responds to sentiment reversal from positive to negative; if sentiment turns negative after a rally, reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 5–10 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently under-estimates true price by 2–8% in the first 10 days; apply a 2–5% upward bias to first 10 days of forecast.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed, model tends to over-smooth price; apply a 1–3% upward adjustment to forecast if sentiment shows any upward momentum.
- Model often lags sentiment shifts by 1–3 days; if sentiment turns positive, delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days to avoid premature overreaction.
